habitat: Singly or in pairs at forest fringes, in riverine forest and in broad-leaved woodland in moister regions.
summary: A common localised resident. More dumpy than Spotted Flycatcher, with duskier underparts and faint smudges rather than streaks. The immature is like the adult. The calls are a thin zeeet and a tsi-ri-rt. The Kemp name Dusky Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

underparts.pattern: Duskier than Spotted Flycatcher, with faint smudges rather than streaks.

viewNotes.note: Dumpy, with duskier underparts and faint smudges.

calls.description: A thin sibilant zeeet and a characteristic tsi-ri-rt. The grade A call is from near Great Brak River. The filename is XC1163086-260222-081842-ADFlycatcher-A.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common localised resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Duskier is not a colour name. The grade A call is from the Western Cape. The Kemp name Dusky Flycatcher and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^10=1024 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 512–2048.
